title: Distribution failure and losing about ten thousand dollars
summary: Airplay on WYLD, but pressing plant delays killed sales; he lost close to ten thousand dollars.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, we did... What were you thinking when you made these records? Did you have any idea once you made them... Yeah. How you were going to market them?
No. See, I wasn't thinking about it. I just said, this is good material. I thought if you just make something with good material, the public ahead won the radio. Now, W.Y.L.D. played it a lot.
Played which record?
All of my records.
All of your records. Okay.
But I didn't have the distribution.
Well, you must have had some local... You must have had some local distributor handling...
Yeah, Joe Banaszczak.
Okay. So, you must have... And if you had Airplay, you must have gotten some sales.

Yeah, I had some sales. See, I didn't know anything about the business. See, when I... The first shipment that I had, those records went just like that. And the people wanted more... The record dealers wanted more records. And I didn't have enough to supply them. And by the time I did find out how to go about getting some more records, it was too late because... See, when you went like... I wanted 500 records pressed.
Right.
And you come up there and say, look, I want 5,000 records pressed, but send it to me right away. They're going to put my little 500 aside.
Right.
And they kept putting mine aside until I didn't... The people that stopped wanting it.
Mm-hmm. You mean the pressing plant.
Yeah.
The plant.
Yeah, the plant. It's like the pressing plant, like if you go there when they are very busy, they're not going to press 500 records.
Right. Right.
Especially if somebody wants 5,000.
Right. Makes a lot of sense.
See, I didn't know all that at that time.

So, you kind of were the babe in the woods, so to speak, when it comes to... When it came to doing, you know, taking care of the record business. So, I mean, you knew how to make the music, but not how to market it. Right. Did you have a partner? Did you have anybody working with you to do promotion?
All by myself.
What year was Pontchartrain? Was this label? Was this... Do you remember what year?
Okay, Wallace Davenport, Reel 5, November the 14th, 1995. Oh yeah, we're going over some more. So the whole investment in the record business was, I mean, how much money do you think you lost?
Yeah, I lost about, I lost close to $10,000. You know, paying the studio time, paying the musicians, and having the records pressed.
